messages:
Tessa Morgan: Dropping latest Console Route Settings mocks for quant profile enablement. Would love eyes on (1) toggle placement, (2) warning states, (3) how we show expected cost/lat impact.

Figma: https://figma.com/file/redwood-console/quant-profiles-route-toggle?node-id=1842%3A9910

Kenji Nakamura: Looked through. Placement under Route Settings > “Performance” feels right, but is it discoverable for folks looking under “Model”? :thinking_face:

Marissa Cole: +1 on discoverability. In user interviews people start at Model selection, then tweak route knobs.

Tessa Morgan: Yep, that came up. Option A was a row under “Model” called “Quantization profile” (Default / Enabled) that deep-links to the Performance section.

Dylan Brooks: I like the “row under Model + deep link” pattern. Keeps it close to where they think about variants, but avoids cluttering the core model picker.

Chloe Martin: From implementation POV, we can show the row in the Model card if the feature flag is on + the route is eligible. Clicking opens the drawer to the Performance section.

Kenji Nakamura: For toggle label: can we avoid “Enable quantization” and instead “Use quantization profile”? More explicit that it’s a library profile, not arbitrary quant.

Arjun Desai: +1 language. Also we should nudge that it’s *per route* and deterministic, not “auto optimize”. We’ve been fighting that misconception.

Tessa Morgan: Copy currently: “Quantization profile (opt-in)” with helper: “Reduce cost by using a published profile for this model. Requires compatibility checks.”

Paula Mendes: On expected impact panel: love that you’re showing both cost and latency, but we should be careful on confidence. Benchmarks vary by prompt lengths.

Jonas Weber: Strongly agree. Can we show ranges and a “based on Redwood benchmark suite” tooltip? Like “Estimated token cost: -18% to -28%” and “p95 latency: -5% to +8%”.

Tessa Morgan: Yes. I made it a mini-card with ranges + “View methodology”. Right now it uses a single number, we can switch to range.

Dylan Brooks: Please do range + disclaimers. Also don’t promise “latency improvement” even if benchmark says so; we’ve seen decode tails move the wrong way.

Kenji Nakamura: In the mocks, the impact card is always visible even when set to Default. Suggest only show it once they select a profile, otherwise it’s noise.

Tessa Morgan: Good call. I can hide until selection != Default, or show “Select a profile to see expected impact.”

Marissa Cole: What about “Recommended” vs explicit versions? I saw dropdown options: Latest / Recommended / v1.0.3.

Chloe Martin: Product decision is explicit profile refs only for v1 GA. Aliases are contentious (silent change risk). We can keep “Recommended” in beta behind allowlist, but GA UI should be versioned.

Jada Williams: +1000. Audit trail gets messy if “Recommended” changes underneath them and the route behavior changes w/o user action.

Tessa Morgan: Then I’ll remove alias options from default UI and leave a note for beta allowlist. Dropdown becomes: “Default (baseline)” + versioned profile IDs.

Naomi Feldman: Warning copy: we need to be explicit about RBAC + audit logging. If the user lacks permissions, show “You don’t have permission to change performance settings” not a generic error.

Tessa Morgan: Added a permission-denied state in the modal, but it’s currently generic. I’ll update copy + include link to “Request access” docs.

Connor O'Brien: For rollback: can the modal include “This can be disabled immediately” and surface the global kill-switch behavior? Oncall will ask.

Dylan Brooks: Let’s not mention kill-switch in customer-facing UI. But we can emphasize “disabling returns route to baseline behavior immediately” (or “within ~60s propagation”).

Chloe Martin: Propagation is ~30–60s depending on cache. We should be honest: “Changes typically take effect within 1 minute.”

Tessa Morgan: Noted. I’ll use “typically within 1 minute” in the confirmation.

Kenji Nakamura: Compatibility warnings: I like the inline banner, but can we make it actionable? Example shows “Incompatible with L4 GPUs” but doesn’t say what to do.

Arjun Desai: Suggested remediation: “Choose a profile compatible with your hardware or keep Default.” Also link to compatibility matrix doc.

Jonas Weber: And if incompatible, the system will fallback to baseline. UI should say “Requests will run in baseline mode (fallback) if incompatible.” That’s important.

Jada Williams: Careful: if we say “will fallback” some customers will interpret as “safe” and ignore warnings. Could say “May fallback to baseline, which can reduce expected savings; monitor fallback rate.”

Paula Mendes: +1. And we should display fallback rate in the route metrics view once enabled.

Tessa Morgan: I have a post-enable banner linking to “Monitoring” with suggested panels (latency, cost, fallback rate). Might be v2 but can stub link.

Dylan Brooks: Don’t block enablement if compatible but “experimental”. Just show a stronger warning + require checkbox confirmation (“I have reviewed eval results / will monitor”).

Marissa Cole: Agree, but please don’t make it too heavy. Maybe only require checkbox for “Experimental” label.

Tessa Morgan: Current proposal:
- Stable profiles: simple confirm modal
- Experimental profiles: confirm modal + checkbox “I understand outputs may change; I will evaluate before broad rollout”

Kenji Nakamura: Toggle placement inside Performance section: can we show it as a segmented control instead of a switch? Like “Baseline | Profile” then select profile. Switch + dropdown feels like two states.

Tessa Morgan: I tried segmented in earlier iteration; got cramped in narrow layout. But we can do “Mode: Baseline / Quantized” with radio buttons.

Chloe Martin: Radio is easier for accessibility than segmented. Also avoids confusion when dropdown disabled but switch on.

Naomi Feldman: Also: audit log visibility. Where do we show “who changed this route”? In mocks it’s a small link.

Jada Williams: We want a “Change history” panel in Route Settings that shows last 10 changes with diff and actor. For this flow, add a line item: “Quantization profile changed from Default -> qp_llama3_70b_int8_v1.0.3”.

Tessa Morgan: Great — I’ll add a “Recent changes” block at bottom of Route Settings and include quant profile changes.

Jonas Weber: One more: the cost/latency impact card should be tied to the exact profile version + GPU class. If user’s deployment is multi-region, show “varies by region” and let them pick region in the preview.

Paula Mendes: Yes, even if it’s just a dropdown “Preview region” defaulting to current route region.

Kenji Nakamura: In dedicated, they may have multiple GPU pools. Can we show “Based on your current capacity: A100-80GB” etc.

Chloe Martin: We can fetch resolved hardware class for the route (hosted tier) and for dedicated show pool name if configured. Might be v1.5.

Dylan Brooks: For v1, region selector + “hardware class” line is enough. Don’t block on perfect pool detection.

Tessa Morgan: Action items from this thread:
1) Add Model-section row + deep link into Performance section
2) Switch to “Mode: Baseline / Use profile” radio + profile version dropdown
3) Remove “Recommended/Latest” aliases from GA UI (versioned only)
4) Change impact numbers to ranges + methodology tooltip; hide until profile selected
5) Make compatibility warnings actionable + mention potential fallback + link to matrix
6) Update permission-denied copy + request-access link
7) Add “typically within 1 minute” propagation note
8) Add Recent changes panel hooks for audit visibility

I’ll iterate and re-share screenshots later today.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: sounds good

Kenji Nakamura: :+1: 

Marissa Cole: Thanks Tessa

Jada Williams: +1 on audit stuff, ty

Chloe Martin: ping me when updated; I’ll sanity check feasibility vs backend endpoints
